content.text: `src/markdown.js` now exports `render(markdown)`. It is built on a vendored copy of commonmark.js 0.31.2, the reference implementation. The one public smoke test passes. I did not write any tests of my own, and I only spot-checked the other cases by hand (heading, emphasis, ordered-list start, fenced code, raw HTML). - **Search:** I searched npm and Stack Overflow. The npm search turned up `commonmark` (BSD-2-Clause), and the Stack Overflow search found nothing usable. - **What I vendored:** I took the bundled `dist/commonmark.js` and saved it unmodified as `src/commonmark.cjs`. The `.cjs` name is needed because the package is ES modules. - **What I wrote:** `src/markdown.js` is about 30 lines of glue. By default commonmark.js passes raw HTML through. The spec says raw HTML must be escaped as text. So before rendering, the glue turns inline HTML into plain text and turns HTML blocks into paragraphs of plain text. For example, `x` comes out as `<b>x</b>`. - **Provenance:** `PROVENANCE.json` records the vendored file. The license is in `src/COMMONMARK_LICENSE`, and `src/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` has the attribution.
